thread.title: If investors had any concerns that 2017’s strong equity mark

author: Dave Dierking, CFA
title: If investors had any concerns that 2017’s strong equity mark
text:
If investors had any concerns that 2017’s strong equity market returns had the ability to carry over into 2018, I think it’s safe to say that they’re probably gone now. The S&P 500 set its 14th all-time high of the year on Friday, and we’re not even to the end of January yet. The Dow and S&P 500 are up more than 7% on the year, and the Nasdaq is up nearly 9%. 
Market watchers Friday were hoping for a third straight quarter of 3% annualized GDP growth. While they didn’t get their wish (the final number came in at 2.6%), there was a lot to like in the report. Consumer spending, construction and investment all showed strong gains. The data did, however, suggest a pickup in inflation, which should cement another rate hike come March. The Fed futures market has priced in a roughly 80% chance of a hike, but the latest data should help push that closer to 100%. 
For now, the bulls continue to remain in firm control, but keep an eye on Tuesday’s State of the Union to see if anything changes! 
Here are your four ETFs to keep an eye on this week! 
iShares U.S. Technology ETF ( IYW ) 
It’s a big earnings week and there’s no bigger sector impacted than technology. Apple ( AAPL ), Facebook ( FB ), Alphabet ( GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) all report this week, and happen to be the four largest holdings in this ETF. They comprise 43% of the fund’s total assets, so expect some potentially big moves from this fund. Tech has continued to roar in 2018, and given that upwards of 80% of companies have beaten earnings expectations, it’s reasonable to think that this fund could be headed up this week.
